compatibility.title: Which Alfa Romeo Models Use the 955A6000?
compatibility.intro: The 955A6000 (and its sister codes 940A3000 and 198A2000) was introduced in 2009 as part of Fiat's second‑generation Multijet diesel family. It appears across Alfa Romeo's compact and crossover ranges, as well as in various Fiat and Lancia models under different codes.

costGuide.title: Alfa Romeo 955A6000 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 955A6000 typically takes 8-10 hours at £65-£75/hr (independent Alfa Romeo specialist) - main dealer rates are significantly higher.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the DPF and EGR system - both are expensive to replace and can be clogged on higher‑mileage cars. The timing belt service history is also critical: this is an interference engine, and a snapped timing belt will destroy the engine. A used unit with documented belt replacement will command a premium. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Alfa Romeo 955A6000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: DPF and EGR System Clogging - urban driving issues
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the 955A6000's diesel particulate filter (DPF) and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system can become clogged, especially with short journeys and urban driving. Early versions (pre‑2014) had an EGR valve that was prone to cracking, though this was improved post‑2014 with additional cooling. Symptoms include reduced performance, poor fuel economy, and warning lights.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning or replacement (£500-£1,200) and EGR cleaning or replacement (£200-£500) can resolve the issue. Regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration is essential. Read our full DPF and EGR guide

items.title: Fuel Injector Failure - rough running and smoke
items.whatHappens: The 1.6 JTDm's common‑rail fuel injectors are known to fail, particularly on higher‑mileage examples. Symptoms include rough idle, misfires, excessive smoke, poor fuel economy, and hard starting. Injector failure can lead to bore wash and cylinder damage if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement (£200-£500 per injector) can resolve the issue if caught early. If injector failure causes bore wash, the engine typically requires full replacement. Read our full injector failure guide

items.title: Timing Belt Failure - snapped belt and bent valves
items.whatHappens: The 1.6 JTDm uses a timing belt, not a chain. Failure to replace the belt at the recommended interval (every 4-5 years or 60,000-100,000 miles) can result in a snapped belt. The engine is an interference design - pistons hit valves, bending them and requiring extensive cylinder head work or full engine replacement.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing belt replacement is essential preventative maintenance (£400-£800). If the belt snaps while driving, the engine is typically destroyed - full replacement is the only option. Read our full timing belt failure guide

items.title: Dual Mass Flywheel (DMF) Rattle
items.whatHappens: The 1.6 JTDm is paired with a dual mass flywheel, which can develop play and rattle over time. Symptoms include a rattling noise on startup or at idle, which disappears when the clutch is depressed.
items.repairVsReplace: DMF replacement is a significant job (£500-£1,200) and should be undertaken when the clutch is being replaced.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 955A6000
variants.intro: The 955A6000 is part of Fiat's second‑generation Multijet diesel family. buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 955A6000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 1.6 JTDm can seem tempting at £800-£1,500, but carries significant risk. You don't know the condition of the DPF, EGR valve, injectors, timing belt, or dual mass flywheel - all of which can fail on higher‑mileage units. A used engine with 60,000+ miles and no documented service history is a gamble. If you must buy used, insist on documented proof of timing belt replacement and regular oil changes using the correct 5W‑30 low‑SAPS oil.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** For most 955A6000 replacements, a professionally reconditioned unit is the right call. A proper recon addresses the engine's known weak points: the timing belt and tensioner are replaced, injectors are tested or replaced, the DPF and EGR are cleaned or replaced, the water pump is replaced, and all gaskets and seals are renewed. With a 12‑24 month warranty, this is the lowest‑risk option for a £1,500-£3,500+ investment.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for this engine only when the original block is in good condition and the vehicle has significant sentimental value - or if a specialist has confirmed that the engine can be saved with new internals. Expect £2,500-£4,500+ for a full rebuild. For most owners, a reconditioned exchange unit offers better value and less downtime.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All reconditioned and rebuilt 955A6000 units can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Alfa Romeo specialists, with nationwide delivery and a minimum 12‑month warranty on every installation. **VEHICLE VALUE NOTE (mandatory):** The 955A6000 sits in vehicles ranging from £3,000-£7,000 (higher‑mileage MiTo, early Giulietta) to £10,000-£18,000+ (low‑mileage, well‑specified Giulietta and Stelvio). A reconditioned unit at £1,500-£3,500+ represents 15-40% of the vehicle's value on most hosts - generally within the replacement‑viable threshold. However, on a sub‑£3,000 example, evaluate the overall vehicle condition and service history before committing; a used unit with documented service history may be the more pragmatic choice.

items.answer: A reconditioned 955A6000 costs £1,500-£3,500+ supply‑only, plus £520-£780 for fitting at a specialist Alfa Romeo workshop. items.question: What are the common problems with the 955A6000?
items.answer: The most significant issues are DPF and EGR clogging (especially in urban use), fuel injector failure, timing belt failure (if maintenance is neglected), and dual mass flywheel (DMF) wear. The EGR valve was prone to cracking on pre‑2014 units, though this was improved post‑2014 with additional cooling. Regular motorway driving is essential for DPF regeneration. Timing belt replacement every 4-5 years or 60,000-100,000 miles is critical.
bullets: Regular motorway driving is essential for DPF regeneration.
Timing belt replacement every 4-5 years or 60,000-100,000 miles is critical.

items.question: Which Alfa Romeo models have the 955A6000 engine?
items.answer: The 955A6000 is fitted to the Alfa Romeo MiTo (2009-2015), Giulietta (2010-2020), and in select markets, the Stelvio (2017-present). It produces 105 hp in the MiTo and early Giulietta, and 115-120 hp in later applications. It was replaced by the 2.0 JTDm in the Giulia and Stelvio in most markets. items.question: Should I buy a used, reconditioned, or rebuilt 955A6000?
items.answer: For most owners, a reconditioned unit offers the best balance - it includes new timing belt, injectors (tested/replaced), DPF and EGR cleaned/replaced, and a 12‑24 month warranty. Used units are cheaper but carry risk of DPF/EGR and injector issues; full rebuilds are justified only if the original block is salvageable. Reconditioned from £1,500; used from £800; rebuilt from £2,500. A used engine without documented DPF and injector service history is a significant risk.

items.question: How do I tell the 955A6000 apart from the 940A3000 and 940C5000?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block (typically on the front or side of the engine), and appears on the V5C and in the VIN. The 955A6000 is a 1.6 JTDm variant (105-120 hp). The 940A3000 is the 105 hp variant in early Giulietta; the 940C5000 is the updated 113-120 hp variant (2015-2018) with improved EGR cooling. All share the same Multijet II architecture but have different ECU and emissions hardware. Fitting the wrong variant can cause ECU and emissions compatibility issues.
bullets: All share the same Multijet II architecture but have different ECU and emissions hardware.
Fitting the wrong variant can cause ECU and emissions compatibility issues.

items.question: How reliable is the 955A6000 compared to the older 1.9 JTDm?
items.answer: The 955A6000 is generally considered more refined and fuel‑efficient than the older 1.9 JTDm, but the modern emissions systems (DPF, EGR) introduce additional failure points. The 1.9 JTDm is simpler and more robust, with fewer DPF issues, but is less economical and emits more CO2. The 1.6 JTDm also has a smaller displacement, which can make it feel less responsive in heavier vehicles like the Stelvio. Regular servicing and using the correct 5W‑30 low‑SAPS oil are critical. Proactive DPF regeneration (motorway driving) is essential.
